name: Hydrogen
description: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe, making up about 75% of all normal matter by mass.

name: Helium
description: Helium is the second-lightest element and the second most abundant in the observable universe. It is an inert, monatomic gas used in cryogenics and as a lifting gas.

name: Lithium
description: Lithium is a soft, silvery-white alkali metal and the lightest solid element. It is widely used in rechargeable batteries and mood-stabilising pharmaceuticals.

name: Beryllium
description: Beryllium is a hard, lightweight, steel-grey alkaline earth metal used in aerospace structures, X-ray windows, and as a neutron moderator in nuclear reactors.

name: Boron
description: Boron is a metalloid found in borosilicate glass, cleaning products, and as a dopant in semiconductors.

name: Carbon
description: Carbon is the foundation of organic chemistry, existing in many allotropes including diamond, graphite, graphene, and fullerenes, and is central to all known life.

name: Nitrogen
description: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere as the diatomic gas N2. It is essential to life as a component of amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids.

name: Oxygen
description: Oxygen is the third-most abundant element in the universe and essential for respiration in most living organisms. It supports combustion and is the most common element in Earth's crust.

name: Fluorine
description: Fluorine is the most electronegative and reactive of all elements. It is a pale yellow diatomic gas used in Teflon production, refrigerants, and uranium enrichment.

name: Neon
description: Neon is an inert, monatomic noble gas best known for the bright reddish-orange glow it emits in vacuum discharge tubes, used in neon signs.

name: Sodium
description: Sodium is a soft, silvery-white highly reactive alkali metal essential to life and abundant in sea salt. It is used in street lighting, soaps, and as a heat transfer medium.

name: Magnesium
description: Magnesium is a shiny grey solid and the eighth most abundant element in Earth's crust. It is essential for life, used in lightweight alloys, and burns with a brilliant white flame.

name: Aluminium
description: Aluminium is a silvery-white, soft, low-density post-transition metal. It is the third most abundant element in the crust and is widely used in packaging, construction, and aerospace.

name: Silicon
description: Silicon is a hard, brittle crystalline solid metalloid and the second most abundant element in Earth's crust. It is the principal material of most semiconductor devices.

name: Phosphorus
description: Phosphorus exists in several allotropes: white, red, and black. It is essential to all known life as part of DNA, RNA, ATP, and bones.

name: Sulfur
description: Sulfur is a bright yellow crystalline solid known since antiquity as brimstone. It is used in gunpowder, rubber vulcanisation, and the manufacture of sulfuric acid.

name: Chlorine
description: Chlorine is a yellow-green diatomic gas with a strong irritating odour. It is widely used as a disinfectant in water treatment and in producing PVC and many industrial chemicals.

name: Argon
description: Argon is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere. It is an inert noble gas used as a shielding gas in welding and in incandescent light bulbs.

name: Potassium
description: Potassium is a soft, silvery-white alkali metal that oxidises rapidly in air. It is essential for the functioning of all living cells and is used heavily in fertilisers.

name: Calcium
description: Calcium is the fifth most abundant element in Earth's crust. It is essential for bones, teeth, and many cellular processes, and occurs widely as limestone and marble.

name: Scandium
description: Scandium is a silvery-white transition metal occasionally used in aerospace alloys to improve strength and in high-intensity discharge lamps.

name: Titanium
description: Titanium is a lustrous transition metal with low density and very high strength. It is corrosion-resistant, biocompatible, and used in aerospace, medical implants, and pigments.

name: Vanadium
description: Vanadium is a hard, silvery-grey transition metal rarely found pure in nature. It is used to make hard steel alloys for tools and springs.

name: Chromium
description: Chromium is a steely-grey, lustrous, hard transition metal valued for its high corrosion resistance. It is used in stainless steel, decorative chrome plating, and pigments.

name: Manganese
description: Manganese is a hard, brittle, silvery metal essential to iron and steel production. It is also a trace nutrient required by all known living organisms.

name: Iron
description: Iron is the most common element on Earth by mass, forming much of the planet's outer and inner core. It is the principal ingredient in steel and essential in haemoglobin.

name: Cobalt
description: Cobalt is a hard, lustrous, silver-grey transition metal used in magnetic alloys, lithium-ion batteries, and historically as a blue pigment in glass and ceramics.

name: Nickel
description: Nickel is a silvery-white lustrous transition metal with a slight golden tinge. It is widely used in stainless steel, coins, and rechargeable nickel-metal hydride batteries.

name: Copper
description: Copper is a soft, malleable, ductile transition metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity. One of the few metals that can occur in nature in a directly usable metallic form.

name: Zinc
description: Zinc is a bluish-white, lustrous transition metal used primarily for galvanising steel to prevent corrosion and as an alloy in brass and bronze.

name: Gallium
description: Gallium is a soft, silvery post-transition metal that melts in the hand. It is used in semiconductors, LEDs, and infrared optics.

name: Germanium
description: Germanium is a lustrous, hard, greyish-white metalloid important in fibre optics, infrared optics, and solar cells.

name: Arsenic
description: Arsenic is a metalloid that exists in many allotropic forms. Its compounds are highly toxic and have been used historically as poisons and in pesticides.

name: Selenium
description: Selenium is a nonmetal with properties between sulfur and tellurium. It is used in photocells, glassmaking, and as an essential trace element for animals.

name: Bromine
description: Bromine is one of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature. It is a reddish-brown fuming liquid with a strong disagreeable odour.

name: Krypton
description: Krypton is a colourless, odourless, inert noble gas present in trace amounts in the atmosphere. It is used in some high-performance light bulbs and lasers.

name: Rubidium
description: Rubidium is a soft, silvery-white alkali metal that ignites spontaneously in air. It is used in atomic clocks and as a getter in vacuum tubes.

name: Strontium
description: Strontium is a soft silver-yellow alkaline earth metal. Its compounds give a brilliant red colour in fireworks and it is used in CRT displays.

name: Yttrium
description: Yttrium is a silvery transition metal used in phosphors for colour displays, in YAG laser crystals, and in certain high-temperature superconductors.

name: Zirconium
description: Zirconium is a strong, malleable transition metal resembling titanium. It is used in nuclear reactor fuel cladding due to its low neutron absorption cross-section.

name: Niobium
description: Niobium is a soft, grey, ductile transition metal. It is used primarily in steel alloys and in superconducting magnets for MRI machines and particle accelerators.

name: Molybdenum
description: Molybdenum has one of the highest melting points of all elements. It is used in high-strength steel alloys, catalysts, and as a lubricant at high temperatures.

name: Technetium
description: Technetium is the lightest radioactive element with no stable isotopes. It is widely used in medical imaging as a radioactive tracer.

name: Ruthenium
description: Ruthenium is a rare, hard, silvery-white transition metal of the platinum group. It is used in electronics, catalysis, and to harden platinum and palladium alloys.

name: Rhodium
description: Rhodium is a rare, silvery-white, hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal. It is used in catalytic converters and as a reflective layer on mirrors.

name: Palladium
description: Palladium is a rare, lustrous silvery-white metal. It is widely used in catalytic converters, electronics, dentistry, and in hydrogen storage.

name: Silver
description: Silver has the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any metal. It has been used for coinage, jewellery, and mirrors for millennia, and today in electronics and solar cells.

name: Cadmium
description: Cadmium is a soft, bluish-white transition metal similar to zinc. It is toxic and is used in rechargeable nickel-cadmium batteries and in pigments.

name: Indium
description: Indium is a soft, malleable post-transition metal that produces a high-pitched cry when bent. It is used in LCDs as indium tin oxide and in low-melting alloys.

name: Tin
description: Tin is a silvery, malleable post-transition metal that resists corrosion. Used since the Bronze Age, today it appears in solders, tin plating, and superconductor alloys.

name: Antimony
description: Antimony is a lustrous grey metalloid. It is used in flame retardants, lead-acid batteries, and historically in cosmetics and medicines.

name: Tellurium
description: Tellurium is a brittle, mildly toxic, silver-white metalloid. It is used in alloys with copper and steel and in cadmium telluride solar panels.

name: Iodine
description: Iodine sublimes to a violet gas and is essential for thyroid hormone production. It is used as an antiseptic and in X-ray contrast media.

name: Xenon
description: Xenon is a colourless, dense, odourless noble gas. It is used in high-intensity arc lamps, ion thrusters for spacecraft, and as a general anaesthetic.

name: Caesium
description: Caesium is a soft, gold-coloured alkali metal that is liquid near room temperature. The SI second is defined by the caesium-133 hyperfine transition.

name: Barium
description: Barium is a soft, silvery alkaline earth metal. Barium sulfate is used as a radiopaque contrast agent for X-ray imaging of the digestive system.

name: Lanthanum
description: Lanthanum is a soft, malleable, silvery-white metal that gives its name to the lanthanide series. It is used in camera lenses and as a catalyst in oil refining.

name: Cerium
description: Cerium is the most abundant of the rare-earth elements. It is used in catalytic converters, lighter flints, and self-cleaning oven coatings.

name: Praseodymium
description: Praseodymium is a soft silvery lanthanide used to colour glass yellow-green and in NdFeB rare-earth magnets.

name: Neodymium
description: Neodymium is a silvery-white lanthanide. Neodymium magnets are the strongest type of permanent magnets commercially available.

name: Promethium
description: Promethium is a radioactive lanthanide with no stable isotopes. It is used in luminous paint and as a beta source in nuclear batteries.

name: Samarium
description: Samarium is a moderately hard silvery lanthanide used in samarium-cobalt magnets that can withstand high temperatures and in cancer treatment.

name: Europium
description: Europium is the most reactive of the lanthanides. It is used as a red and blue phosphor in television screens and energy-saving fluorescent lamps.

name: Gadolinium
description: Gadolinium is a silvery-white, malleable lanthanide. Its compounds are used as contrast agents in MRI scans and in neutron shielding.

name: Terbium
description: Terbium is a silvery-white lanthanide used as a green phosphor in trichromatic lamps and in solid-state devices.

name: Dysprosium
description: Dysprosium is a soft, silvery lanthanide added to neodymium magnets to improve their performance at high temperatures.

name: Holmium
description: Holmium has the highest magnetic strength of any naturally occurring element. It is used in nuclear control rods and in the strongest magnets known.

name: Erbium
description: Erbium is a silvery-white lanthanide used in fibre-optic communication amplifiers, which are essential for the internet.

name: Thulium
description: Thulium is the second-least abundant lanthanide. It is used in portable X-ray devices and as a dopant in solid-state lasers.

name: Ytterbium
description: Ytterbium is a soft, malleable, silvery lanthanide used in fibre lasers, atomic clocks, and as a dopant in stainless steel.

name: Lutetium
description: Lutetium is the last and hardest of the lanthanides. It is used in PET scan detectors and as a catalyst in petroleum cracking.

name: Hafnium
description: Hafnium is a lustrous, silvery transition metal resembling zirconium. It is used in nuclear reactor control rods and in high-temperature alloys.

name: Tantalum
description: Tantalum is a rare, hard, blue-grey transition metal highly resistant to corrosion. It is used in electronic capacitors and surgical implants.

name: Tungsten
description: Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals. It is used in incandescent light bulb filaments, X-ray tubes, and cutting and drilling tools.

name: Rhenium
description: Rhenium is a silvery-white, heavy transition metal and one of the rarest elements in Earth's crust. It is used in high-temperature superalloy turbine blades.

name: Osmium
description: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element. It is a hard, brittle, bluish-white metal used in fountain pen tips and electrical contacts.

name: Iridium
description: Iridium is the most corrosion-resistant metal known. It is used in spark plugs, crucibles, and as a hardener for platinum.

name: Platinum
description: Platinum is a dense, malleable, ductile, highly unreactive precious metal. It is used in catalytic converters, jewellery, laboratory equipment, and electrical contacts.

name: Gold
description: Gold is the most malleable and ductile of all metals. It is used in coinage, jewellery, electronics, dentistry, and as a monetary reserve.

name: Mercury
description: Mercury is the only metallic element liquid at standard conditions. It is silvery-white, toxic, and used in thermometers, barometers, and some electrical switches.

name: Thallium
description: Thallium is a soft, malleable post-transition metal. It is highly toxic and was historically used as a rodenticide and in insecticides.

name: Lead
description: Lead is a soft, dense, malleable, toxic post-transition metal. It has been used for thousands of years in plumbing, paint, and as a gasoline additive.

name: Bismuth
description: Bismuth is a brittle, silvery-white post-transition metal with a pinkish hue. It is used in low-melting alloys, cosmetics, and stomach medicines.

name: Polonium
description: Polonium is a highly radioactive, extremely toxic element with no stable isotopes. It has been used as a heat source in satellites.

name: Astatine
description: Astatine is the rarest naturally occurring element. It is intensely radioactive and only minute amounts have ever been produced.

name: Radon
description: Radon is a colourless, odourless, radioactive noble gas formed from radium decay. It is the leading cause of lung cancer among non-smokers.

name: Francium
description: Francium is an extremely rare, highly radioactive alkali metal. Only trace amounts have ever existed, so little is known about its bulk properties.

name: Radium
description: Radium is a radioactive alkaline earth metal discovered by the Curies. It glows blue in the dark and was historically used in luminous paint.

name: Actinium
description: Actinium is a radioactive metal that glows blue in the dark due to its intense radioactivity. It is used as a neutron source and in targeted alpha therapy.

name: Thorium
description: Thorium is a weakly radioactive actinide. It is being researched as a potential nuclear fuel alternative to uranium.

name: Protactinium
description: Protactinium is a dense, silvery-grey radioactive actinide. It is one of the rarest and most expensive naturally occurring elements.

name: Uranium
description: Uranium is a silvery-grey radioactive actinide. It is the main fuel used in nuclear power reactors and was used in the first atomic bombs.

name: Neptunium
description: Neptunium is a radioactive actinide produced in nuclear reactors. It was the first transuranium element to be synthesised.

name: Plutonium
description: Plutonium is a radioactive actinide used in nuclear weapons and as a fuel in some nuclear reactors. It is also used in cardiac pacemakers.

name: Americium
description: Americium is a synthetic radioactive actinide. It is used in household smoke detectors as the alpha particle source.

name: Curium
description: Curium is a hard, dense, silvery radioactive actinide named after Marie and Pierre Curie. It is used as a power source in space missions.

name: Berkelium
description: Berkelium is a synthetic radioactive actinide named after Berkeley, California. It has no commercial applications outside of basic research.

name: Californium
description: Californium is a strong neutron emitter used in nuclear reactor start-up, as a moisture neutron source in oil well logging, and in cancer treatment.

name: Einsteinium
description: Einsteinium was first identified in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb test. It is used only in basic scientific research.

name: Fermium
description: Fermium was discovered in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb. It is the heaviest element that can be formed by neutron capture.

name: Mendelevium
description: Mendelevium is a synthetic radioactive actinide named after Dmitri Mendeleev. It can only be produced in microscopic quantities.

name: Nobelium
description: Nobelium is a synthetic radioactive actinide named after Alfred Nobel. It has no practical applications beyond research.

name: Lawrencium
description: Lawrencium is the final member of the actinide series. It is a synthetic radioactive element with no practical applications.

name: Rutherfordium
description: Rutherfordium is a synthetic radioactive transition metal. It is the first transactinide element and is named after Ernest Rutherford.

name: Dubnium
description: Dubnium is a synthetic radioactive transition metal named after Dubna, Russia. It has no practical applications.

name: Seaborgium
description: Seaborgium is a synthetic radioactive transition metal named after Glenn T. Seaborg. It was the first element named after a living person.

name: Bohrium
description: Bohrium is a synthetic radioactive transition metal named after Niels Bohr. Only a few atoms have ever been produced.

name: Hassium
description: Hassium is a synthetic radioactive transition metal named after the German state of Hesse. Only a few atoms have been produced.

name: Meitnerium
description: Meitnerium is a synthetic radioactive element named after Lise Meitner. Its chemical properties have not been conclusively established.

name: Darmstadtium
description: Darmstadtium is a synthetic radioactive element named after Darmstadt, Germany. Only a few atoms have been produced.

name: Roentgenium
description: Roentgenium is a synthetic radioactive element named after Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen. Its chemical properties are expected to be similar to gold.

name: Copernicium
description: Copernicium is a synthetic radioactive element named after Nicolaus Copernicus. It is expected to behave as a volatile liquid metal.

name: Nihonium
description: Nihonium is a synthetic radioactive element named after Japan (Nihon). It is the first element discovered in Asia.

name: Flerovium
description: Flerovium is a synthetic radioactive element named after the Flerov Laboratory. It may have unusual noble-gas-like properties.

name: Moscovium
description: Moscovium is a synthetic radioactive element named after Moscow. Its chemical properties are expected to be similar to bismuth.

name: Livermorium
description: Livermorium is a synthetic radioactive element named after Livermore, California. Its predicted properties are similar to polonium.

name: Tennessine
description: Tennessine is a synthetic radioactive element named after Tennessee. It is the second-heaviest element ever created.

name: Oganesson
description: Oganesson is the heaviest known element, named after Yuri Oganessian. It is a synthetic radioactive element with unusual predicted properties.
